cards.title: The culture surrounding 'ideal' childbirth has to evolve
cards.body: Letters respond to an article about a five-day labour, with an NHS doctor sharing her personal experience of feeling 'othered' during childbirth. The discussion highlights how cultural expectations around 'ideal' birth experiences need to change.

cards.title: Parenting is hard. Should we let AI do it for us?
cards.body: Tech companies offer eye-movement trackers, personalized podcasts and 'optimized nap predictions' for parents. The article questions whether parents actually need these AI tools or if they're just adding to parenting pressure.

cards.title: Should I try the '18 summers' parenting trend?
cards.body: The '18 summers' trend encourages parents to turn school holidays into intentional 'memory-making' exercises. Critics argue this turns free time into a controlling, stressful experience when kids actually need unstructured play.

cards.title: Why your 'teachable moments' keep backfiring
cards.body: Explaining what went wrong while emotions are still high feels right but often creates intense conflict with children. Better timing and a calmer approach help kids actually learn from mistakes rather than feeling attacked.

cards.title: Why are gifted children, teenagers so intense?
cards.body: Gifted children often display intense emotions and behaviors that baffle parents. Understanding these challenges is the first step toward supporting their unique needs effectively.

cards.title: Stop bankrolling your adult child's stuck life
cards.body: Every financial bailout sends a message to adult children—rarely the one parents intend. Enabling behavior prevents grown children from developing independence and resilience.

cards.title: How much parents could save from September school uniform rules
cards.body: New school uniform rules limit branded items to three pieces plus a tie for secondary schools. This change could significantly reduce costs for families buying back-to-school uniforms.
